 SECTION 1.  Arkansas Code § 5-66-103(a), concerning the offense of 28 
keeping a gambling house, is amended to read as follows: 29 
 (a)  A person or entity commits the offense of keeping a gambling house 30 
if the person or entity: 31 
  (1)  Keeps, conducts, or operates, or who is interested directly 32 
or indirectly in keeping, conducting, or operating any gambling house or 33 
place, whether a physical location or online, where gambling is carried on; 34 
  (2)  Sets up, keeps, or exhibits or causes to be set up, kept, or 35 
exhibited or assists in setting up, keeping, or exhibiting any gambling 36

device; or 1 
  (3)  Is interested directly or indirectly in running any gambling 2 
house or in setting up and exhibiting any gambling device, either by 3 
furnishing money or another article, for the purpose of carrying on any 4 
gambling house; 5 
  (4)(A)  Makes available or participates in keeping, conducting, 6 
or operating any game, contest, or promotion that is available on the 7 
internet or accessible on a mobile phone, computer terminal, or similar 8 
device capable of accessing the game, contest, or promotion that utilizes a 9 
dual-currency system of payment that allows the player to exchange the 10 
currency for a prize, award, cash, or cash equivalent, or a chance to win any 11 
prize, award, cash, or cash equivalent, and simulates: 12 
    (i)  Casino-style gaming, including without 13 
limitation slot machines, video poker, or table games that include without 14 
limitation blackjack, roulette, craps, and poker; 15 
    (ii)  Lottery games, including without limitation 16 
draw games, instant win games, keno, and bingo; and 17 
    (iii)  Sports wagering. 18 
   (B)  A sweepstakes game that does not award cash or a cash 19 
equivalent is not included under subdivision (a)(4) of this section. 20 
   (C)  Subdivision (a)(4)(A) of this section does not apply 21 
to a casino licensed by the Arkansas Racing Commission; or 22 
  (5)(A)  Makes available or participates in keeping, conducting, 23 
or operating any game online that the commission or the Department of Finance 24 
and Administration, consistent with the Arkansas Constitution, may determine 25 
by rule to be sports wagering. 26 
   (B)  Subdivision (a)(5)(A) of this section does not apply 27 
to a casino licensed by the commission or a lottery conducted under the 28 
Arkansas Scholarship Lottery Act, § 23-115-101 et seq. 29

 SECTION 2.  Arkansas Code Title 23, Chapter 117, is amended to add an 31 
additional subchapter to read as follows: 32 
Subchapter 2 — Interactive Gaming Act 33 
 34 
 23-117-201.  Title. 35 
 This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Interactive 36 
As Engrossed:  H3/31/25 H4/1/25 HB1861 
 
 3 04-01-2025 10:23:46 CRH232 
 
 
Gaming Act”. 1 
 2 
 23-117-202.  Definitions. 3 
 As used in this subchapter: 4 
   (1)  "Casino licensee" means any individual, corporation, 5 
partnership, association, trust, or other entity holding a license issued 6 
by the Arkansas Racing Commission to conduct casino gaming as authorized 7 
by The Arkansas Casino Gaming Amendment of 2018, Arkansas Constitution, 8 
Amendment 100; 9 
   (2)  "Dormant account” means an interactive gaming account that 10 
has had no patron-initiated activity for a period of sixteen (16) months; 11 
   (3)(A)  “Interactive gaming” includes the placing of wagers 12 
through a server-based gaming system that is situated in the United States 13 
using a computer network of interoperable packet switched data networks 14 
through which a casino licensee may offer authorized interactive games to a 15 
person who has established an interactive gaming account. 16 
    (B)  "Interactive gaming" includes the placing of wagers 17 
using:  18 
     (i)  A mobile cellular device using an application; 19 
or  20 
     (ii)  An internet browser on a supported device using 21 
software. 22 
    (C)  "Interactive gaming" includes a name, image, or 23 
likeness drawing game conducted through an electronic device or machine to 24 
benefit a name, image, or likeness collective consistent with the Arkansas 25 
Student-Athlete Publicity Rights Act, § 4-75-1301 et seq.;  26 
   (4)(A)  “Interactive gaming system” means a gaming device. 27 
    (B)  "Interactive gaming system" includes:  28 
     (i)  The collective hardware, software, 29 
communication, technology, and proprietary hardware and software specifically 30 
designed or modified for and intended for use in the conduct of interactive 31 
gaming; and 32 
     (ii)  The core components of the interactive gaming 33 
system, including without limitation the servers or databases running the 34 
games on the interactive gaming system and storing game and interactive 35 
gaming account information, that are hosted within the United States, with 36

the core components residing on physical hardware or a remote server, 1 
provided that gaming participation is confined to the state; and 2 
 (5)  "Name, image, or likeness drawing game" means a drawing game 3 
of chance approved by the commission, the net proceeds of which after 4 
incurred expenses, as approved by the commission, are divided between: 5 
  (A)  A name, image, or likeness collective consistent with 6 
the Arkansas Student-Athlete Publicity Rights Act, § 4-75-1301 et seq., or 7 
any other organization affiliated with an Arkansas collegiate athletics 8 
program; and  9 
  (B)  The winning participant. 10

 23-117-203.  Interactive gaming. 12 
 (a)(1)(A)  A casino licensee shall not operate an interactive gaming 13 
system in this state unless the interactive gaming system has been approved 14 
by the Arkansas Racing Commission. 15 
   (B)  An activity conducted under Arkansas Constitution, 16 
Amendment 84, shall not be considered interactive gaming. 17 
  (2)  An interactive gaming system operated by a casino licensee 18 
is subject to rules promulgated by the commission. 19 
  (3)  A casino licensee is limited to one (1) branded interactive 20 
gaming system that is identified with the casino licensee. 21 
  (4)  The operation of interactive gaming is prohibited in 22 
circumstances in which a majority of the net casino gaming receipts, as 23 
defined by The Arkansas Casino Gaming Amendment of 2018, Arkansas 24 
Constitution, Amendment 100, from interactive gaming is paid to a third-party 25 
vendor assisting in the operation of the interactive gaming. 26 
 (b)  An interactive gaming system shall meet applicable minimum 27 
technical standards provided in Gaming Laboratories International's GLI-19: 28 
Standards for Interactive Gaming Systems, as revised on July 17, 2020, or an 29 
equivalent certification issued by a testing laboratory as approved and 30 
licensed by the commission. 31 
 (c)  A casino licensee may operate a name, image, or likeness drawing 32 
game as approved by the commission. 33 
 34 
 23-117-204.  Internal controls for casino licensees related to 35 
interactive gaming.  36 
As Engrossed:  H3/31/25 H4/1/25 HB1861

 (a)  A casino licensee shall comply with:  1 
  (1)  Standards related to interactive gaming adopted by the 2 
Arkansas Racing Commission to implement this subchapter; and  3 
  (2)  Existing rules of the commission.  4 
 (b)  The commission shall:  5 
  (1)  Approve game titles or themes; and  6 
  (2)  Provide for standards and practices consistent with the 7 
standards and practices of the Gaming Laboratories International, or other 8 
testing entity licensed by the commission, approved in another jurisdiction 9 
in the United States to serve as validation in Arkansas. 10 
 (c)(1)  Live personnel engaged in dealing cards or similar activities 11 
involved in interactive gaming shall hold a gaming license in the 12 
jurisdiction in which the live personnel physically operate. 13 
  (2)  A casino licensee shall transmit a list of the live 14 
personnel described in subdivision (c)(1) of this section to the commission 15 
no less than monthly. 16 
 (d)  The commission may determine additional areas that require 17 
internal controls that may necessitate the development of minimum standards. 18 
 19 
 23-117-205.  Acceptance of wagers. 20 
 A casino licensee shall not accept or facilitate a wager on interactive 21 
gaming other than as set forth by rule of the Arkansas Racing Commission. 22 
 23 
 23-117-206.  Disposition of dormant accounts.  24 
 (a)(1)  A casino licensee may suspend a dormant account.  25 
  (2)  The casino licensee may reactivate a dormant account 26 
suspended under subdivision (a)(1) of this section only after reverifying the 27 
current government-issued picture identification of the account holder and 28 
other information as required by the Arkansas Racing Commission.  29 
 (b)  All amounts remaining inactive in the dormant account after a 30 
period of two (2) years of the account's becoming a dormant account shall be 31 
paid into a cash fund of the commission.  32 
 (c)  Before closing a dormant account under this section, the casino 33 
licensee shall attempt to contact the account holder a minimum of one (1) 34 
time per year. 35

 23-117-207.  Prohibition — Penalty. 1 
 (a)  The operation of an interactive gaming system without a casino 2 
license in this state is prohibited. 3 
 (b)  Consistent with § 5-66-103, a violation of subsection (a) of this 4 
section is a Class D felony. 5 
 6 
 23-117-208.  Rules. 7 
 The Arkansas Racing Commission may promulgate rules to administer and 8 
enforce this subchapter. 9 
 10 
 SECTION 3.  EMERGENCY CLAUSE.  It is found and determined by the 11 
General Assembly of the State of Arkansas that unlicensed, unregulated, and 12 
untaxed casino style and sports wagering offerings are an ever-growing threat 13 
to the citizens of Arkansas.  Further, institutions of higher education and 14 
their affiliated nonprofit organizations are intertwined with economic 15 
development, the education of student-athletes, commerce, and other 16 
governmental interests that otherwise impact the State of Arkansas; that a 17 
drawing game conducted through interactive gaming, in order to benefit a 18 
name, image, or likeness organization, the net proceeds of which, after 19 
incurred expenses, are equally divided between a name, image, or likeness 20 
organization and the participant, can increase economic development, 21 
education, and commerce in the State of Arkansas; and that this act is 22 
immediately necessary to ensure that institutions of higher education and 23 
their affiliated nonprofit organizations can financially support their 24 
student-athletes and athletic programs, which will bolster economic 25 
development, education, and commerce in the State of Arkansas.  Therefore, an 26 
emergency is declared to exist, and this act being immediately necessary for 27 
the preservation of the public peace, health, and safety shall become 28 
effective on: 29 
  (1) The date of its approval by the Governor; 30 
  (2) If the bill is neither approved nor vetoed by the Governor, 31 
the expiration of the period of time during which the Governor may veto the 32 
bill; or 33 
  (3) If the bill is vetoed by the Governor and the veto is 34 
overridden, the date the last house overrides the veto. 35
